cohort: 748 pregnant women at 12 weeks gestation or more.
finding: Detection of clue cells at 20% or more appeared to be the most promising diagnostic tool for bacterial vaginosis with a sensitivity of 87.1%, specificity of 55.8%, positive predictive value of 31.2%, negative predictive value of 95.0%, diagnostic odds ratio of 8.57, accuracy of 61.6, and Youden index of 0.43.
